questions_json.explanation: Unexpected panic attacks plus ongoing worry about more attacks and avoiding places where they might occur is the classic picture of panic disorder.
questions_json.q: Ali has sudden attacks of racing heart, sweating, and a feeling of dying. The attacks come out of nowhere, and now he avoids shopping malls fearing another attack. What is the most likely diagnosis?

questions_json.explanation: MDD requires 5 or more symptoms for at least 2 weeks, with depressed mood or loss of interest (anhedonia) as one of them.
options: At least 5 symptoms for 2 weeks including depressed mood or loss of interest
questions_json.q: Sara has felt sad almost every day for three weeks, lost interest in everything, sleeps 12 hours a day, and cannot concentrate on her studies. What must be true for a diagnosis of major depressive disorder?

questions_json.explanation: A manic episode (no sleep, grandiosity, risky spending) plus a history of depression points to bipolar I disorder — one manic episode alone is enough for the diagnosis.
questions_json.q: Omar has not slept in 4 days, talks nonstop, spent all his savings on a new business, and believes he will soon be famous. Last year he was deeply depressed for months. Which disorder fits best?

questions_json.explanation: Hallucinations, delusions, and disorganized speech are positive symptoms — extra experiences added by the disorder, unlike negative symptoms which take things away.
questions_json.q: Hassan hears voices commenting on his actions and believes the TV sends him secret messages. His speech jumps between unrelated topics. These are examples of which symptom group?

questions_json.explanation: The intrusive thought about germs is the obsession; the repeated washing done to reduce the anxiety is the compulsion.
options: Washing her hands 40 times a day
questions_json.q: Fatima washes her hands 40 times a day. She knows it is excessive but cannot stop because the thought 'germs will kill my family' terrifies her. Which part is the compulsion?

questions_json.explanation: Intrusion (nightmares), avoidance, and arousal symptoms lasting more than one month after trauma fit PTSD — acute stress disorder lasts under a month.
questions_json.q: After a car accident, Ahmed has nightmares about the crash, avoids driving, and dives under tables when he hears loud brakes. His symptoms started 3 months ago and disrupt his life. What is the likely diagnosis?

questions_json.explanation: Repeated binge episodes with distress but no purging or compensatory behavior is binge-eating disorder — bulimia nervosa requires purging.
questions_json.q: Ayesha eats huge amounts of food alone at night twice a week and feels deep shame, but she never vomits or over-exercises afterward. Her weight is normal. Which eating disorder fits best?

questions_json.explanation: Unstable relationships, frantic fear of abandonment, impulsivity, self-harm, and chronic emptiness are the hallmarks of borderline personality disorder.
questions_json.q: Maria idealizes her new friend as perfect on Monday but calls her cruel on Wednesday for replying late. She fears abandonment, harms herself when upset, and feels empty inside. Which personality disorder fits?

questions_json.explanation: Needing more for the same effect is tolerance; physical symptoms when stopping are withdrawal — both are key criteria of substance use disorder.
questions_json.q: Khan needs twice as much alcohol as last year to feel the same effect, and he shakes and sweats when he skips drinking for a day. What do these two signs indicate?

questions_json.explanation: Talking about being a burden, giving away possessions, and sudden calm after depression are serious warning signs — take them seriously, stay with the person, and connect them to help immediately.
options: Tell him to just think positive
Take it seriously and stay with him while getting help
Ignore it so you don't encourage him
Wait a few days to see if he improves
questions_json.q: Your friend says 'Everyone would be better off without me,' gives away his favorite books, and has become suddenly calm after weeks of depression. What is the best first response?
